llmshield.title: LLMShield
llmshield.summary: A security gateway prototype that inspects messages, applies configurable policy decisions, and records audit metadata without storing raw prompts or responses by default.
capabilities: FastAPI chat endpoint with an OpenAI-style, non-streaming response envelope.
Heuristic checks for selected prompt-injection phrases, email and phone patterns, and selected secret formats, including common Unicode obfuscation.
Validated YAML policy configuration with allow, redact, block, and review actions, plus enforce and monitor modes.
Local deterministic mock provider; external model forwarding is disabled by default.
SQLite metadata-only audit events and an authenticated operational metrics endpoint summarizing recent decisions, finding categories, and severities.
React dashboard, Docker Compose setup, regression tests, and a synthetic evaluation harness.
evidence: Repository README documents setup, architecture, policy configuration, evaluation, and limitations.
The synthetic evaluation reports precision, recall, false-positive rate, and false-negative rate per detector category; its small synthetic dataset is diagnostic, not a real-world benchmark.
limitations: Detection is heuristic and can miss attacks or flag benign text.
Real provider forwarding, streaming, and a human-review queue are not implemented.
Redaction is not complete anonymization; shared-key authentication is a baseline rather than a full identity system.

cloudsentry.title: CloudSentry
cloudsentry.summary: A local-first static configuration auditor for selected security patterns in Terraform, Dockerfiles, and Docker Compose.
capabilities: Ten documented rule IDs across Terraform, Dockerfiles, and Docker Compose.
Findings include severity, confidence, evidence, impact, remediation, fingerprints, and source locations.
CLI reports in text, JSON, and SARIF 2.1.0, plus a local FastAPI API and React + TypeScript dashboard.
SARIF invocation diagnostics preserve scan warnings and errors; machine-readable reports retain suppression justifications.
Dashboard distinguishes Complete, Partial, and Error scans, supports search and severity filtering, and allows suppressed findings to be inspected.
Reason-required, narrow suppressions; incomplete scans take exit code 2 rather than being presented as clean.
evidence: Repository README documents CLI usage, dashboard setup, exit codes, responsible use, and limitations.
Regression tests cover SARIF output, suppression behavior, source attribution, and CLI integration paths.
limitations: Static checks are heuristic and need contextual review; a clean scan does not prove a configuration is secure.
Terraform checks do not resolve variables, locals, modules, dynamic blocks, provider defaults, or effective permissions.
The dashboard API accepts local filesystem paths and should remain bound to loopback for local development.
